properties.name: Imzouren Fault
properties.notes: May be at the next terrace flight down

properties.name: Amekchoud-Imidir Thrust
properties.reference: Pastor et al., 2012 Annals of Geophysics

properties.name: Jebel Guersif Thrust
properties.notes: Thrust breaks through anticline; Teson has another blind thrust ~~200 m south. He also has a steep (~30° ramp soling into a 5 flat at sea level.
properties.reference: Teson et al., 2008 Int. J. Earth Sci.

properties.name: Midelt Thrust
properties.notes: Good expression of scarp on DEM.

properties.name: Ait Oufella Frontal Thrust
properties.notes: Balanced X-Sec shows a flat at 1 km above sea level ~5 degree).

properties.name: Ait Oufella Frontal Thrust
properties.notes: little transfer structure

properties.name: El Ksabi Fault
properties.reference: DEM; Gomez et al. 1996 J. Geo. Soc. London

properties.name: South Middle Atlas Frontal Thrust
properties.notes: Blind thrust; anticline is very well exposed. Likely merges with South Middle Atlas Thrust at depth.

properties.name: Beni-Mellal Fault
properties.notes: Lithologic boundary that likely corresponds to older rift-bounding normal fault. Could be steep, could be shallow.

properties.name: Tigheboula Thrust
properties.notes: frontal nappe-bounding thrust to main Beni-Mellal thrust

properties.name: South Middle Atlas Rangefront Thrust
properties.notes: Rangefront thrust; may not be currently active, but basinward blind thrusts probably sole in at ~1 km depth or so. May be steep reactivated rift-bounding normal fault, or may be shallower thrust.

properties.name: South Middle Atlas Frontal Thrust
properties.notes: Blind thrust and anticline.
Possible blind thrust in basin.

properties.name: Tsouaint-Arhal-Tamdafelt Anticline
properties.reference: Laville et al., 2007 Int. J. Earth Sci., Pastor et al., 2015 Tectonophysics

properties.name: Kasbah Thrust
properties.notes: Some surface rupturing during the 1960 Agadir earthqake, which may or may not have been on a ramp of this fault at depth to the north.

properties.name: South Atlas Thrust
properties.notes: Blind?

properties.name: South Atlas Thrust
properties.notes: No clear rupture but some possibilities. Also some evidence of folding/ blind thrusting into the basin.
Spotted on DEM and Google Earth.

properties.name: North Atlas Fault
properties.notes: Rangefront fault, mostly (some deformed rocks to north). No idea if it's active or where the trace is, mapped mostly from DEM.
Front of uplifted fan basinward of the North Atlas Fault.  Looks more active than rangefront fault but this is a tricky orogen.

properties.name: North Atlas Fault
properties.notes: Strange triangular bedrock salient at North Atlas rangefront. Possibly a nappe.

properties.name: Nekor Fault
properties.notes: sinistral-normal in NE, sinistral-reverse in SW

properties.name: Fez Fault
properties.notes: Signs of active deformation and GPS gradient at approx. location of frontal thrust of the Rif belt. The Rif structures look very thin-skinned, however, some of the structures observed in the DEM look to be strike-slip. Things are unclear.
properties.reference: DEM, drawn approx. on many maps

properties.notes: Possible trace observed by linking geomorphic features on DEM. Essentially at the southern Rif thrust front, but may not be reactivating old thrust. Some GPS velocity gradient. City of Fez is at western end, should be a primary target of field investigation.

properties.name: Sanhaja Fault
properties.notes: Very well expressed lineament in DEM; worth investigation
Hosted the 1999 Ain Temouchent earthquake; good InSAR study.
Looks like an active thrust w/ a rapidly-subsiding hanging-wall basin. No clear scarps but the HW is so smooth and there are no fans so it looks like the HW is dropping fast.

properties.name: Mohammadia Thrust
properties.notes: Some signs of warping of Quaternary seds at rangefront, but otherwise looks like  a thrust w/ a rapidly-subsiding foreland. Links up w/ other thrusts and folds (blind thrusts) in many places.

properties.name: Murdjadjo Thrust
properties.notes: Bouhadad located field exposures w/ 60 degree dip. This may not characterize the whole structure.

properties.name: Bou Kadir Fault
properties.notes: Possible sinistral component
properties.reference: Aifa and Idres, 2010 Open Geology Journal

properties.name: El Asnam Fault
properties.notes: Ruptured in the M7.1-7.3 El Asnam Earthquake
Possible fresh scarp at base (visible in 30m DEM)

Looks like a reverse or oblique-reverse thrust. Not sure of what strike-slip direction, but it's oblique to other thrusts. Could be either based on stress/convergence directions. Basin looks like it's subsiding relatively rapidly but otherwise not a lot of evidence for recent faulting.

properties.name: Sahel Thrust
properties.notes: Rupture traces visible in DEM east of big canyon in middle. Apparent left-lateral offset of drainages across the fault.

properties.name: Mitidja Thrust
properties.notes: Ruptured in the 2003 Zemmouri earthquake (M6.8), 0.5 m slip.
Consistent pattern of right-offset stream drainages. Looks like a dextral fault that swings around into a thrust. The high topo in hanging wall may not be coincidental.

properties.name: Berda Thrust
properties.notes: Blind
Blind
blind
Unclear if it's active; geomorphically distinct but not evidence HW subsidence.  Some EQs in area.

properties.name: Soummam Fault
properties.notes: Minor Quaternary offset observed in field (by Machane and Bensalem), though it's hard to tell tectonic scarps from fluvial features in DEM

properties.name: Kherrata Fault
properties.notes: Very unclear where the active Kherrata Fault is in particular (clearly there are many in the vicinity), to what degree any of them are active, or their rates and kinematics. Nonetheless it's referenced a bit and there is seismicity in the region.
Shown in general on lots of maps. Precise location uncertain, activity uncertain, etc...

Shown on lots of maps, with general DEM expression (but no clear fault trace). No idea if it's active, although there is distributed local strike-slip seismicity consistent with dextral slip on a structure like this.

properties.name: Guelma Fault
properties.notes: Shown on lots of maps, but actual fault trace (or existence of active faulting) is very unclear.
Best-expressed normal fault in the Atlas. Dextral-normal faulting in graben.

properties.name: Tebessa Fault
properties.notes: 5.4 EQ on fault in 1995

properties.name: Khmouda Fault
properties.notes: Neogene? graben. Looks active, but slow.
good geomorphic expression. Possibly some normal fault (down to the south) slip as well.
Maybe active... Was certainly active in Neogene, but Quaternary activity uncertain.

properties.name: N-S Axial Fault
properties.notes: Blind oblique-reverse (?) fault under major regional fold. A fair amount of associated seismicity, but it looks like an inverted (or reactivated) basement structure.  It's in a lot of papers but no good surface break.

properties.name: N-S Axial Fault
properties.notes: Blind reverse-oblique (?) fault below well-defined anticline. Lots of associated moderate seismicity but kinematics and geometry a little unclear.

properties.name: Western Fault
properties.reference: Abdunasser and McCaffrey 2015 J. Earth Systems Science

properties.name: Eastern Fault Zone
properties.notes: Fault geomorphology nice in the south but gets a bit ambiguous towards the north.

properties.name: Markha Baba transfer Fault
properties.notes: May be oblique
Gets a little ambiguous towards the north and south. Might not be very active.

properties.name: St. Anthony Fault
properties.notes: Some scarps in Google Earth. Strange structure.
Can't find any real scarps in Google Earth but could be marginally active
Gorgeous tectonic geomorphology in DEM and Google Earth
well-observed in bathymetry
Mw 6.4 on 2016-01-25 in GCMT catalog
A combination of bathymetric interpretation and dextral faults in the literature that have no real geomorphic or seismic expression
Mauffret connects to the Thenia Fault onshore along strike, although this would curt what are known to be larger active thrusts.
poorly drawn w/ wrong strike-slip kinematics in Mauffret, based on newer data
May have been responsible for 2003 Bourmedes EQ or some aftershocks
Another likely offshore reverse fault with possible dextral slip
Doesn't look active as nearby traces but fills in a deformation gap and there is a basin (maybe old?)
westernmost Rif thrust. It's got to be somewhere and this is a convenient topographic escarpemnt.
Westernmost Rif thrust; hard to place trace exactly but seismicity and GPS stop here
Koulali has it mapped (from earlier sources?) but does not draw a GPS block boundary along it. Nonetheless there  is a ~1mm/yr velocity gradient across it.

properties.name: Kalabsha Fault
properties.notes: Basement structure that shows mild deformation of Cenozoic sediments above. Thought by Kebeasy to be the host of teh 1981 Aswan earthquake; those papers are unavailable to me but they found evidence fro ground deformation. The Aswan earthquake is widely believed to be from elevated stresses and fluid pressure following the filling of Lake Nasser.
properties.reference: DEM; Mekkawi et al., 2005 EPSL; Kebeasy et al., 1987
